name: Offline lifecycle harness
description: Runs the real poller, executor, persona resolver, folder sync, scheduling helper and lane helpers against a fake client and a scripted model, with no model calls.
advantages: Deterministic and free coverage of the whole lifecycle including duplicates, lost claims and team scoping. Selected because: runner/config_wiring.py (a lane's run_lane drives Poller and TaskExecutor)
disadvantages: The fake client hides wire-level behaviour such as HTTP errors and real payload shapes, and crash recovery of orphaned claims is not yet covered.

name: Two small model verdicts when a goal is created (today)
description: On a shared quest, a small model names the likely assignee and judges doability for an AI representative.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: Task poller and claimer
description: Discovers due tasks per scan, deduplicates by signature across restarts, claims through the backend, hands each task to the executor with bounded concurrency, and pauses pickup when the host is overloaded.
advantages: Event-driven, restart-safe, and degrades instead of crashing on transient errors.
disadvantages: Large and stateful, with several guards that interact, so edge cases such as orphaned claims are hard to see.

name: Single-task executor
description: Runs one claimed task through the orchestrator and maps the result onto a status report: answer or met deep run is done, a short deep run is incomplete or failed, a decision is needs-you, a cancelled task gets no report. It never raises to the poller.
advantages: One clear unit of work that is easy to test with a mock client and stub brain.
disadvantages: The mapping from result to status is policy that must stay in step with the backend's status vocabulary.

name: Shared lane entry point
description: Provides the check, once and loop-forever driver with argument parsing, env-file loading, local-time due gating and degrade-instead-of-crash behaviour on incomplete config.
advantages: Removes the duplicated glue each consumer used to write.
disadvantages: Consumers must fit its argv shape, and the local-time gate patches behaviour globally.

name: Universal guidance provider
description: Merges file-based guidance cards with dynamic guidance from feedback and rep profiles, scores them by tags, keywords and optional vector similarity, optionally filters with a model, and returns the top few for injection. It re-reads dynamic sources each selection so new feedback appears at once.
advantages: One provider covers static policy and learned corrections, supports semantic selection, and picks up change without restart. Selected because: RunnerConfig.guidance_provider
disadvantages: Without a vector or model filter it has no relevance cut under the card limit, so unrelated rules can show. Model filtering adds latency and cost.

name: Live ledger and provider arm
description: Replays correction and turn steps through the real feedback ledger, run-account receipt and guidance writer, then runs a real orchestrator with the real provider and reads the guidance block from the planner prompt it sent. Only the model is scripted.
advantages: Tests the true loop end to end for recall and precision at no model cost, and was clearly best of the three arms.
disadvantages: Shares the live weakness on precision, and a scripted model says nothing about whether a real model obeys the guidance.

name: No-feedback floor
description: An assistant that hears corrections and forgets them: no later turn is shown anything, so it never leaks and never repeats.
advantages: Zero cost and perfect precision by construction, which isolates the value of the loop.
disadvantages: Recall is nil, so every correction must be made again; it is the worst arm on the repeat-correction rate.

name: Show-everything baseline
description: Remembers every correction verbatim and shows all of them on every later turn, with no ledger, no standing-versus-one-off distinction and no relevance.
advantages: Perfect recall and trivially simple, so it shows what the real loop must beat on precision.
disadvantages: One-off requests become permanent rules and unrelated rules crowd every prompt, growing the prompt without bound.

name: Host chat classifier among assigned representatives (today, in the host)
description: The host's chat picks among the quest's assigned representatives the person can see with one fast-model call, falling back to the person's default representative.
advantages: Built; cheap; respects per-viewer visibility; only assigned representatives are candidates.
disadvantages: Lives in the host, not the library; unmeasured; the tasks a chat spawns may run as someone else.

name: A thread keeps its representative (proposed)
description: Proposed. Once a thread has a representative, every task and pass it spawns runs as that representative unless the person names another, and the choice is recorded on the task.
advantages: Removes the one-thread, many-voices failure seen in production; no model call.
disadvantages: A task that truly needs another representative's role must be named explicitly; not built.

name: Fit by role, assigned quests and intent branch (proposed)
description: Proposed. Among a quest's assigned representatives, the one whose role text and assigned quests (and the intent branch they sit in) best cover the request is chosen, scored without a model where clear and with one small call on the borderline.
advantages: Uses what the host already stores; ties the choice to whose higher mind fits the request.
disadvantages: Free-text roles are uneven; borderline cases cost a call; not built.

name: Ask the person on an equal fit (proposed)
description: Proposed. When two representatives fit equally, the person is asked once which should handle it, and the answer is remembered for that kind of request on that quest.
advantages: Never guesses on a real tie; the answer becomes a label.
disadvantages: Each question costs the person attention; must stay rare; not built.

name: Work-folder sync
description: Mirrors a work item's state and notes into a local file with runner-managed marked sections, and pushes new human notes back once, preserving human-authored text elsewhere in the file.
advantages: Idempotent, keeps human edits, and uses only the existing client methods.
disadvantages: A single shared file can conflict with hand edits near the markers, and direction rules must be respected by callers.

name: Decision-request sink
description: Adapts the Quest client into the escalation port: it resolves an assignee (explicit, then default, then the quest owner), refuses to file an unaddressed ask, applies a deadline default, and creates a hold-default team decision request whose identifier it returns. Before it files, it puts the ask to the hub's Judgment Calls (hubofhubs.run, the selected arm; signal: the ask's severity and summary, person: the resolved assignee, context: needs a person): on ask it files and keeps the timing for the caller (a high severity blocks the run, anything else waits while the work that does not depend on the answer continues), on proceed or decline under a person's own policy it files nothing and says so, and a judgment that fails never loses the ask. The create_decision operation a worker calls makes the same call and tells the worker what the timing means. Standing work (a run the autopilot composed) raises its own ask through that operation and keeps working; in a thread turn with a person waiting the runner raises the one ask.
advantages: Never files an ask nobody will see, and puts decisions where the team already works. Selected because: RunnerConfig.escalation (defaults to QuestDecisionSink)
disadvantages: Tied to one backend's decision model, and a missing owner or backend failure surfaces as an error rather than a quiet fallback.

name: Fake-backend delivery check
description: Runs the production sink against an in-memory fake client, checking the assignee fallback chain, kind, default, deadline, review link, team routing, repeated asks and backend failure.
advantages: Offline and exact about what was filed and to whom.
disadvantages: Scores delivery and detail only, not whether the brain chose to escalate, and the fake cannot show real backend behaviour.

name: Conversation screen (Textual)
description: This package's own Textual screen: a chat with saved conversations, a conversation picker, personas from the corpus, a model-tier menu, a command menu, a trail of the work and ask folds, and run control for a deep turn. About 9,700 lines under the_consciousness/terminal. Scored on the requirements of the hub's page by tests/test_terminal_requirements.py.
advantages: Complete for conversation: saved and resumable conversations, personas, tiers, the Quest commands.
disadvantages: Its generic parts (screen, input line, transcript, run control) are a second copy of what the hub's terminal now holds; 6 of the 23 requirements unmet (X8 one helper stopped alone, X9 a risky step waiting for the answer, X11 harness switch, X13 plain output and replay, X22 a question answered while the run goes on, X23 no restated settings).

name: Conversation in the hub's selected terminal (opencode)
description: This package's attended conversation drawn by the terminal the hub selected, the stock opencode client, through the hub's library entry point (`host_in_opencode`): each message is one run of the orchestrator's stream (grounded in the matched or selected quest, kept like the Textual screen's turn), the header says the quest, the persona, the model and the line of saved notes the turn looked at, the slash commands are the session's own handlers (`/quest` lists and selects, `/rep`, `/reps`, `/file`, `/model`, `/save`, `/load`, `/sessions`, `/status` and the rest of the supported set), and the client's model picker lists auto, the hub's tiers and the models it serves. A note typed while it works steers the live worker. The default of `chat` when the client is installed (`--screen auto`); `QAR_SCREEN=chat` or `--screen chat` keeps the Textual screen, which is also the fallback when the client is missing or of another major version.
advantages: Gets the hub's selected terminal (tabs, its keys, its look) with this package's quests, personas and commands, and nothing generic is kept here.
disadvantages: No numbered pickers, panels or keys of the Textual screen (/pause, /resume, /trace, /updates, /continue, the sources panel): those stay on the Textual screen. Needs the client installed (tested version named by the hub).

name: The hub's terminal with this package's binding
description: The hub's Terminal Experience (its selected arm: a Textual screen, the standard-library one where Textual is missing) with this package's words, the person the AI acts for and the lane's ceilings supplied through the hub's binding points. Runs a goal on a real harness while the person watches, stops, resumes and steers it; a line after a run is a follow-up. Opt in with `quest-ai-runner chat --screen hub`.
advantages: Meets the requirements the conversation screen misses and shares its screen, keys and controls with every other consumer of the hub; nothing generic is kept here.
disadvantages: No counterpart yet for saved conversations, the picker, corpus personas or the model-tier menu, so it is not the default of `chat`.
